summary: Check the Codex app-server traffic against the JSON schema the installed CLI generates. The schema parts we use are committed with a regeneration script; tests fail when what codex-adapter.ts and the usage probes send or read differs from it. Fixes the one drift found: item/permissions/requestApproval was answered with a decision instead of a granted permission profile.

reactNativeIos.reason: The Expo app does not speak the Codex app-server protocol. It sees Codex approvals only as backend request.opened events, whose shape this change does not touch; Approve and Deny reach the same respondToRequest path.

nativeAndroid.reason: The native Android app does not speak the Codex app-server protocol. It sees Codex approvals only as backend request.opened events, whose shape this change does not touch; Approve and Deny reach the same respondToRequest path.

storageDataMigration.reason: No stored data changes. Pending approvals live in memory per session, and the new answer builder is kept beside them, not persisted.

automated: Mutation checks, reverted: renaming turnId on turn/interrupt and clientInfo on the usage probe's initialize fails the tests; answering a permissions request with a decision fails them.
hardware: node scripts/codex-app-server-schema.mjs against codex-cli 0.162.1 (installed) and 0.160.1 (official npm darwin-arm64 package, temp dir), both with a throwaway CODEX_HOME; the two extracts differ only in fields we neither send nor read.
notExercised: No live Codex session raised item/permissions/requestApproval; the new answer is checked against the schema only.
Remote machines pin codex 0.153.2 (provision-setup.ts); its schema was not generated, so the permissions answer is not verified there.
The *_READS tables are kept by hand; a new read the adapter adds is checked only once it is listed there.
